messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

A working machine and keeping this from becoming a fight are what I need. I’m not sure how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up. Your shared-list approach sounds fair; I can’t take on chasing people or arranging the repair.

You’re not reading that wrong—I wouldn’t want B to feel her dad’s machine is being dismissed. The leak needs addressing, but I’m also hoping for something with less upkeep day to day. I can’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota, so a straightforward plan would help. I’m not sure what parts of the old setup could be kept.

You’re not reading that wrong. I want it repaired and kept—not because replacement cost is settled, but because it was Dad’s, and letting it go feels like losing a piece of him. I’d accept a proper repair if it stops the leak and is practical to maintain. I don’t have much time, so this needs to fit into small slots; I also don’t want it breaking constantly and wearing me down. Let’s not decide by who replies first or make A feel outvoted.

My part of the list sounds right. I can’t confirm the details about C or B beyond knowing B wants to keep Dad’s machine. I can’t say about paying until there’s a cost and proposed share, and I’m not sure I can be there for the visit. Keeping the old machine rather than scrapping it would help it feel less dismissed, though I can’t speak for B.

The parts about C and A’s limits aren’t things I know, so don’t list them as confirmed on my say-so. The rest of my concern is right, though I’d add that keeping the old machine unrepaired as a keepsake isn’t what I’m asking for.

I can make one service visit if it’s scheduled in a small slot. Someone else can be there, too, if they share what the technician finds. Keeping Dad’s machine untouched while a simpler one takes over wouldn’t feel like enough to me—but I’d consider it after we know whether a proper repair is practical.

That’s right about me. I’m fine with a visit on a day that suits A or B, if they arrange it. I can share the findings with both if I receive them. I still don’t know how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up.

I’d appreciate you arranging the one visit; I’d rather not take that on. I’m not sure how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up. I can’t promise I’ll be there, and I don’t know yet whether a weekday morning or afternoon works—please check with B too.
I don’t know how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up. Please arrange the visit as your one-off help. An afternoon suits me better; I can make a short slot if it’s scheduled ahead.
Yes, that’s fine, as long as the findings are shared with both A and B. I don’t need to be the one relaying them.

Thanks, this sounds like a reasonable way forward. I don’t know how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up, but I’ll check with B before the visit. We can discuss costs once we have a figure. I understand you’re only helping with the one visit.
Understood. I can make a short afternoon slot. I still don’t know how bad the leak is or who’s cleaning it up; I’ll check with A and C before the visit. Thanks for arranging it.
Understood. If I receive the findings, I’ll share them with both; otherwise A or B can pass them on. I can’t take on ongoing follow-up.
Understood. If I receive the findings, I can pass them on once to B and C, but I can’t take on ongoing follow-up. I’ll check with B about the leak and cleanup.
Understood. If I receive the findings, I’ll pass them to A and C. I’ll check with them about the leak and cleanup before the visit.
